section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section summarizes the findings of 'This study' regarding age and gender differences in the association between gratitude and loneliness. It confirms that greater daily gratitude is generally linked to less loneliness (Hypothesis 1). The study also found that this association varies by age and gender, being stronger in younger women than men, but stronger in older men than women (Hypothesis 2). The section highlights that age is associated with greater benefits from gratitude, particularly for older men, and discusses these findings in the context of literature on gender differences in social relationships and aging.

section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses a single study that investigated age and gender differences in the association between gratitude and loneliness. The study found that greater daily gratitude was generally linked to less loneliness (Hypothesis 1). The association varied by age and gender (Hypothesis 2), being stronger in younger women than men, but stronger in older men than women. These findings, illustrated in Fig. 1, are discussed in relation to socioemotional selectivity theory and literature on gender differences in social relationships and aging.
